disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Rhode Island DEM Division of Fish & Wildlife before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.beaver_fisher_permits: Beaver trapping requires a Special Beaver Trapping Permit (no fee) plus pelt tagging (§ 9.14(D)). Fisher trapping requires a Special Fisher Trapping Permit (no fee), pelt tagging, carcass/parts turnover, and a completed fisher trapping log (§ 9.14(E)).
license_summary.hunting_license: A valid Rhode Island hunting license is required to hunt furbearers. Coyote, fox, and raccoon hunting seasons are set in the small-game section (§ 9.12).
license_summary.state_lands: A free Permit to Trap State Management Areas (no fee) from the Division of Fish and Wildlife is required in addition to a trapping license to trap on DEM management areas (§ 9.14(H)). Written landowner permission is required to trap on private land (R.I. Gen. Laws § 20-16-9).
license_summary.trapping_license: A current Rhode Island Trapping License is required to trap furbearers (§ 9.14(A)).
license_summary.trapping_report: Every trapping-license holder must report the number and species of all furbearing animals taken within 30 days of the end of the trapping season; a license will not be renewed until the report is filed (R.I. Gen. Laws § 20-16-12).

sources.notes: Published final regulation text on the RI Government Register. §§ 9.12 (small-game/furbearer hunting seasons) and 9.14 (Furbearer Trapping) are the source of all season dates, zones, bag limits, and tagging rules. Archived locally in hidden_files/season-research/rhode-island/.

permit_requirements: Special Beaver Trapping Permit (no fee) from the Division of Fish and Wildlife, plus a current RI Trapping License (§ 9.14(D)(2)).
All beaver pelts must be presented for tagging as prescribed by the DEM (§ 9.14(D)(1)(a)).

bag_limits.limit_notes: Season bag limit: 40 beaver for Rhode Island resident trappers, 20 beaver for non-residents, per § 9.14(D)(1).

seasons.notes: Beaver trapping season on private land: November 1 to March 14, inclusive. Traps may not be set prior to sunrise on opening day. No traps within 10 feet of a beaver lodge/bank den except under a Division-issued nuisance permit.

bag_limits.limit_notes: Season bag limit: 40 beaver for Rhode Island resident trappers, 20 beaver for non-residents, per § 9.14(D)(1).

seasons.notes: Beaver trapping season on State Management Areas: December 1 to the last day of February, inclusive (Feb 28, 2027). Requires the free Permit to Trap State Management Areas in addition to a trapping license. Traps may not be set prior to sunrise on opening day. No traps within 10 feet of a beaver lodge/bank den except under a Division-issued nuisance permit.

permit_requirements: Special Fisher Trapping Permit (no fee) from the Division of Fish and Wildlife, plus a current RI Trapping License (§ 9.14(E)(2)).
All fisher pelts must be presented for tagging as prescribed by the DEM; no pelt is tagged without submission of the carcass or required parts (§ 9.14(E)(1)(a)-(c)).
All fisher carcasses or required parts, as determined by the Division, must be turned in to the Division of Fish and Wildlife (§ 9.14(E)(1)(b)).
A Division-issued fisher trapping log must be completed and returned at the close of fisher season; failure to submit results in denial of future permits (§ 9.14(E)(3)).

bag_limits.limit_notes: Season bag limit: 1 fisher per § 9.14(E)(1).

seasons.notes: Fisher trapping season: December 1 to December 24, inclusive. The Division reserves the right to alter the number of permits or fishers harvested at any time (§ 9.14(E)(4)).

seasons.notes: Coyote HUNTING season on State lands: September 15 to the last day of February, inclusive. Legal shooting hours 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset. 200 sq in fluorescent orange required Oct (3rd Sat)–Feb; 500 sq in during shotgun deer season. See spring-turkey-season entry for the second State-lands hunting window.

bag_limits.limit_notes: Coyote bag limit unlimited.

seasons.notes: Coyote HUNTING on State lands is also open during the open spring turkey hunting season (§ 9.12(M)): modeled as the union of the 2027 spring turkey seasons — paraplegic weekend Apr 24–25, youth season Apr 26–May 2, statewide season Apr 29–May 23 — i.e. Apr 24–May 23, 2027.

species.notes: No open season on bobcat in Rhode Island (§ 9.14(J)). Included so the app flags any logged take as out of season. A bobcat taken under the depredation provisions (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 20-16-2, 20-16-8) may not be tagged for personal use or ownership and must be presented to the Division of Fish and Wildlife or the Division of Law Enforcement within 24 hours (§ 9.14(K)).

No open season on river otter in Rhode Island (§ 9.14(J)). Included so the app flags any logged take as out of season. An otter taken under the depredation provisions (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 20-16-2, 20-16-8) may not be tagged for personal use or ownership and must be presented to the Division of Fish and Wildlife or the Division of Law Enforcement within 24 hours (§ 9.14(K)).

verification.confirmation_notes: 250-RICR-60-00-9 amendment is ACTIVE with effective date 07/28/2026 per the RI Secretary of State rule register — the regulation governing the 2026–27 season year is final law. All dates transcribed from the final regulation PDF (filed as REG_13477_20260708094201690). The 2026–27 DEM Hunting & Trapping Abstract was not yet published as of 2026-09-18, so no booklet cross-check was possible; the abstract will be verified against this dataset when published. Calendar-verified: first Saturday of November 2026 = 2026-11-07 (fox hunting opener); second Saturday of September 2026 = 2026-09-12 (squirrel hunting opener); last Thursday of April 2027 = 2027-04-29 (statewide spring turkey opener, basis for coyote state-lands spring window).
known_gaps: The DEM-published 2026–27 Hunting & Trapping Abstract was not yet available (the latest found was the 2025–2026 guide). Dates come from the final regulation text alone; re-cross-check against the abstract when it publishes.

Furbearer TRAPPING dates (§ 9.14) are unchanged from prior years: Nov 1–Jan 31 group season, beaver Nov 1–Mar 14 (private) / Dec 1–last-day-of-Feb (State Management Areas), fisher Dec 1–24, coyote private-land year-round.
Fox HUNTING (§ 9.12(J)) changed for 2026–27: first Saturday of November through last day of December (Nov 7–Dec 31, 2026); prior years ran third Saturday of November through last day of February.
The regs print the gray squirrel Latin name as 'Sciuris carolinensis' (misspelled); this dataset uses the correct taxonomy Sciurus carolinensis and flags the discrepancy.
Coyote's scientific name is not stated in the regulations — marked scientific_name_verified=false; all others are stated in the official text (verified=true).
Muskrat has a stated season bag limit (15) but no stated daily bag limit; daily_bag is null with a note.
Beaver season bag limits differ by residency (40 resident / 20 non-resident); modeled as season_bag 40 with an explanatory note.
Gray and red squirrel share a hunting daily bag of 5 (singly or in aggregate); modeled as daily_bag 5 on each species' hunting entry with a note.
Raccoon hunting on Prudence and Patience Islands (Jan 1–Feb 28 with landowner permission) and the bow-hunter exception (Oct 1–Jan 31 during deer shooting hours) are noted, not modeled as zones.

Coyote state-lands hunting 'during the open spring turkey hunting season' is modeled as the union of the 2027 spring turkey season windows (Apr 24–May 23, 2027); if spring turkey dates shift, this entry shifts with them.
Woodchuck (groundhog) is not included: it is not a regulated furbearer for trapping in RI and is covered only by the small-game hunting season (§ 9.12(I)).

Depredation take outside seasons (R.I. Gen. Laws § 20-16-2 — property owners may kill furbearers damaging property, carcass turned over to DFW) is noted but not modeled as a season — the app should offer an override rather than blocking the log.
Trap hardware/placement rules (§§ 9.14(G)-(I), 9.14(N)-(P)) are NOT in this dataset — seasons, zones, limits, and permits only.
